session_title: Project Implementation: Crowdfunding, Sterilization, and Community Conventions

content.text: Yifan, look, the donation chain has started in the community group! Everyone is so enthusiastic. This time, we've raised 500 yuan, which is enough to spay or neuter two or three cats. Remember two months ago in pet_1_01, we were urgently making a warm cat shelter for that mother cat who had just given birth? Now we can finally move forward with the fundamental solution of spaying and neutering.

Great! That's really efficient. I've also found the most cost-effective partner hospital. The total cost for spaying/neutering, vaccination, and post-operative anti-inflammatory treatment per cat is about 150 yuan, which is 20% cheaper than the cheapest option in the comparison table I compiled earlier in pet_1_02. Making the most of our resources, this budget can now cover more cats.

The mother cat has been successfully trapped and is ready to be taken to the hospital. Look, the doctor is very professional, and the cat is calm, so the surgery should go smoothly. This is the mother cat we found in pet_1_01 with three kittens. The kittens have grown a bit, and this time, we’ll spay the mother first.
Okay. That's good. The old towels you collected earlier, the clean ones used in pet_1_01 for making the cat bed, can be used for post-operative care, maintaining a frugal and practical approach.

Okay, I'll keep that in mind. After the surgery, I plan to keep the cat on my balcony. I've already prepared a warm nest, just like the DIY cat bed last time, made from a foam box and old clothes. I'll stick to the foam box insulation method you taught me in pet_1_01—I'm quite familiar with it now.

Making the most of resources is excellent. The surgery costs will be covered by the crowdfunding, and any leftover money can be set aside for future TNR funds. Your organizational skills are truly impressive—you’ve mobilized everything so quickly. Just as you mentioned in pet_1_02, shifting from emergency responses to addressing root causes, and now it’s truly being implemented.

Thanks to the TNR infographic you shared earlier, the neighbors immediately understood its importance. However, relying solely on donations isn’t a long-term solution. I’ve been wondering if we could encourage the property management or the homeowners’ association to take some action? Just like we discussed before, turning individual acts of kindness into community norms.

I have the same idea. We could try to establish a "Civilized Management Convention for Stray Animals in the Community," which would include provisions such as designated feeding points, support for sterilization, and opposition to animal abuse. This would help address the issue systematically and prevent situations like the emergency in pet_1_01, where only temporary measures could be taken during an unexpected cold snap.

Yes! This will help reduce uncontrolled breeding and avoid emergencies like the last late spring cold snap. You have a clear logic—could you help draft an initial version? Just like when you drew design diagrams and created comparison tables in pet_1_01 and pet_1_02, let's organize everything clearly.
I've already drafted one. What do you think of this announcement style? The content is based on your previous experience with community activities, emphasizing practicality and a human touch.

Wow, that was done so quickly! The content is very comprehensive, including fixed feeding points and neutering support. I'll take it to communicate with the property management and try to post it on the community bulletin board.

Okay. Additionally, post-surgery care requires regular wound checks. I've made a simple care guide and sent it to you. You can use old materials to make a homemade head cone to prevent licking—it's both frugal and effective. It’s still our usual DIY approach, just like when I guided you remotely to make the cat bed.

Thank you! The cat has already had the surgery, and the doctor said it went very smoothly. It can be released back in a week. Look, it's eating with a pink cone on its head and seems to be doing well. Thinking back to how it was squeezed on the concrete floor after giving birth to kittens in pet_1_01, it can finally look forward to a healthier future now.

The headgear fits quite well, making the most of it. This crowdfunding and convention advancement make me feel that community mutual aid can truly solve big problems, just like the cat shelter incident before. From pet_1_01's emergency appeal to the current long-term planning, the efficiency optimization is quite evident.

Yes, from emergency assistance to the TNR program, it's all thanks to your technical support and logical analysis. With someone like me who's always worrying, having your help makes things much more reassuring. I still remember in pet_1_01, you called me a "worrywart." Now, that worrying has finally been put to good use, driving systemic change.

Likewise, your practical skills and warm-heartedness are what truly matter. If the convention is passed, we can regularly organize TNR activities and keep the fund rolling. As mentioned in pet_1_02, it's a good start, and indeed, that's how it looks now.

Great idea! I'll schedule a time with the property management to discuss the community guidelines. This first successful TNR case is a good start, and I hope more neighbors will get involved. It feels like we're turning the temporary cooperation of 'mutual assistance and sharing' from pet_1_01 into the long-term 'community belonging' envisioned in pet_1_02.

Well, combining technological democracy with a sense of community belonging leads to greater efficiency. Stay in touch, and feel free to reach out whenever needed. Just as mentioned at the end of pet_1_01, we still need to arrange for neutering, and now we’re truly taking steps to make it happen.

Absolutely! Thank you, Yifan. Let's keep working hard to make our community more harmonious. From that damp, chilly corner over two months ago to now promoting the community covenant, every step has been supported by your technical expertise. It feels truly wonderful.
